brief:
Israel confronts three potential outcomes following its latest election deadlock, according to Middle East Eye. The country could proceed with another Netanyahu-led government, shift toward an Eisenkot minority administration, or return to voters for a fresh round of elections. Each option carries distinct political and institutional consequences as coalition negotiations stall.

The deadlock reflects deepening fragmentation within Israeli politics, with no single bloc commanding a Knesset majority. The coming weeks will determine whether existing parliamentary blocs can forge new coalitions or whether fresh elections become unavoidable.
dek: Israel’s election deadlock: What could happen next? Submitted by Lubna Masarwa on Wed, 10/28/2026 - 16:51 There are three options facing Israel: more Netanyahu, an Eisenkot minority government, or another round of elections.
title: Israel faces three paths amid election deadlock
